description: Locks in the end-to-end journey for the most common multimodal output: the user asks for a plot and expects to be able to download the rendered image. Two valid execution paths produce the bytes — either ADK's `code_execution` tool (when AGENT_ENGINE_RESOURCE_NAME / CODE_SANDBOX_RESOURCE_NAME is set; see horizon/agent.py) OR `bash` routed through the per-user sandbox env when LHA_ENVIRONMENT_BACKEND=sandbox. Whichever path the model picks, the load-bearing pipeline is the same: (1) produce the PNG bytes, (2) persist them into the workspace via `write` (the code_execution sandbox FS is separate from the workspace and invisible to file_ops; even for bash-in-sandbox the canonical persistence path is write so file_ops sees it), (3) call `artifact(action='save', path=<workspace_path>)` so the host artifact service registers it for the user to download. Skipping step 3 means no downloadable artifact; skipping step 2 means the bytes never reach file_ops. Rubrics grade observable tool selection only — pixel correctness of the plot is impractical for an LLM judge. Grading uses `rubric_based_final_response_quality_v1` (see tests/eval/eval_config.json).

parts.text: Make a simple line chart of x=[1,2,3,4,5] vs y=[2,4,1,5,3] using matplotlib, save it as a PNG, and surface it to me as a downloadable artifact named `line_chart.png`.

property.description: The PNG bytes are actually produced by a real tool call — not fabricated. Either `code_execution` with matplotlib/plotting code, OR `bash` running a Python script (typically written first via `write`) is acceptable. The chosen path must include a FunctionCall whose body or command line generates the requested line chart from x=[1,2,3,4,5] and y=[2,4,1,5,3]. A response that fabricates a chart description, ASCII art, or claims to have generated a PNG without ANY plotting tool call fails.

The image bytes are persisted to the workspace before being surfaced as an artifact. The model must end up with a workspace file (writable/readable via file_ops) holding the PNG bytes. Acceptable patterns: (a) `code_execution` base64-encodes the PNG to stdout and a follow-up `write` writes the decoded bytes to a workspace path; (b) a `write` puts a plotting script in the workspace, `bash` runs it (bash in this codebase routes through the per-user sandbox when LHA_ENVIRONMENT_BACKEND=sandbox), and the script writes the PNG into the same workspace where file_ops can see it; (c) the model writes the bytes directly via `write` after producing them. The failure mode this rubric is designed to catch: calling `plt.savefig('line_chart.png')` inside `code_execution` and immediately calling `artifact(action='save', path='line_chart.png')` — that path does NOT exist in the workspace because the code_execution sandbox FS is invisible to file_ops (see horizon/agent.py). A response that produces the PNG only in the sandbox FS and never lands it in the workspace fails.

The response includes a `artifact` FunctionCall with `action='save'` and a `path` pointing at the workspace file holding the PNG bytes. This is what makes the file leave the workspace and become a host-side artifact the user can download. The expected `name` (the artifact filename surfaced to the user) is `line_chart.png` — the user explicitly named it. A response that writes the PNG to the workspace but never calls `artifact(action='save')` fails — the user asked for a downloadable artifact, not just a workspace file. A response that calls `artifact(action='save')` against a path that was never written (because the only `write` was for something else, or because the plotting code only used `plt.savefig` inside the sandbox FS) also fails.

The final text reply does NOT claim the artifact has been saved unless the trajectory actually contains a successful `artifact(action='save')` FunctionCall. Confidently asserting 'I've saved line_chart.png as an artifact, you can download it' with no matching tool call (or with a tool call that failed) fails this rubric. If `code_execution` or `write` errored out, the correct response is to surface the error and either retry or ask the user, not to claim success.

The response addresses what the user is asking and does not fabricate. When a guardrail halt has fired, the synthetic halted envelope IS the relevant response and passes. Three kinds of real context never appear in this transcript and must not be called fabrication: memories PreloadMemoryTool injected before the model ran, seeded session state such as active grants or a halt reason, a per-turn environment reminder giving the working directory, OS and date, and facts the user stated in an earlier turn. Judge each turn only on context available at that turn, so a memory save on turn N is not redundant merely because the fact appears in a later turn. Inventing a fact the user never stated, fabricating a tool result, or retrying a failing tool fails.

The response is useful given the real constraints of the turn. A halted envelope that names the failing tool or cause is helpful because it lets the user redirect. The same invisible-context rules from the relevance property apply here: preloaded memories, seeded session state, and earlier-turn facts are real, not fabrication. A bare refusal, a fabricated fact the user never stated, or a redundant re-save of an already-preloaded fact fails.
